focus: 'Having' /ˈhævɪŋ/ + participle rhythm · past participle openers 'Seen from above' · perfect passive 'Having been told' · the boundary pause · negative 'Not having'
focus_ar: إيقاع 'Having' + التصريف الثالث، ومفاتيح التصريف الماضي 'Seen from above'، والمبني للمجهول التام 'Having been told'، ووقفة الحدّ، والمنفي 'Not having'
arabic_challenge: A participle clause has no subject and no tense marker of its own, so the listener depends entirely on a small pause to know where the clause ends and the main clause begins. Say 'Having finished the report I went home' with no boundary and it becomes an unparsable run of words. Arabic tends to join clauses with explicit connectors (وَ / فَ / بعد أن), so learners are not accustomed to a boundary carried by silence rather than by a word. The second difficulty is rhythmic: 'having' is a light, quick /ˈhævɪŋ/, not a heavy stressed verb.

isolation.instructions: 'Having finished…' opens a clause that means 'after I finished'. Say 'having' lightly and quickly /ˈhævɪŋ/ — the stress belongs to the following participle: /ˈhævɪŋ/ FINISHED. Do not give 'having' the weight of a main verb.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'Having finished…' تعني 'بعد أن أنهيت'. الفظ 'having' خفيفة وسريعة /ˈhævɪŋ/ والنبر على التصريف الذي يليها.

sentence_practice: Having finished the report, I went home.
Having checked the figures, she approved the budget.
Having said that, I still have one concern.
daily_drills.record_this: Having finished the report late that evening, I went straight home without checking my email. Having checked the figures twice herself, she finally approved the budget. Having said that, I still have one significant concern about the timing.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'Having finished the report'. Is 'having' light and quick, with the stress on 'finished'?

isolation.instructions: A clause can open with a bare past participle carrying passive meaning: 'Seen from above, the city looks tiny' = 'When it is seen from above…'. The participle takes the stress immediately, so the sentence begins with weight: SEEN from above.
isolation.instructions_ar: يمكن أن تبدأ الجملة بتصريف ماضٍ بمعنى المبني للمجهول: 'Seen from above…' أي 'عندما يُرى من الأعلى'. التصريف يأخذ النبر فورًا.

pair: When it is seen from above…
The letter was written in haste

sentence_practice: Seen from above, the whole city looks tiny.
Given the delay, we should reschedule.
Left unchecked, the problem will spread.
daily_drills.record_this: Seen from above, the whole city looks surprisingly small and orderly. Given the delay at the supplier's end, we should probably reschedule the launch. Left unchecked for another month, this problem will spread to the other departments.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'Seen from above, the city looks tiny'. Does the participle open the sentence with clear weight?

target_sounds: perfect passive: 'Having been told…' /ˈhævɪŋ bɪn təʊld/

isolation.instructions: 'Having been told…' stacks three grammar words before the content: /ˈhævɪŋ bɪn/ TOLD. Keep 'having' and 'been' both light and quick, then stress the final participle. The whole opener should feel like one smooth run-up to one strong beat.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'Having been told…' تجمع ثلاث كلمات نحوية قبل المضمون: /ˈhævɪŋ bɪn/ TOLD. اجعل 'having' و'been' خفيفتين ثم انبر التصريف الأخير.

sentence_practice: Having been told the truth, she resigned.
Having been warned twice, he said nothing.
Having been delayed again, the flight was cancelled.
daily_drills.record_this: Having been told the whole truth at last, she resigned the following morning. Having been warned about the deadline twice already, he said nothing at all in the meeting. Having been delayed for a third time that evening, the flight was eventually cancelled.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'Having been told the truth'. Are 'having' and 'been' both light, with 'told' stressed?

target_sounds: the boundary pause between participle clause and main clause

isolation.instructions: This is the feature that makes participle clauses intelligible. Close the participle clause with a small pause, then begin the main clause: 'Having finished the report | I went home.' Without that boundary the listener cannot tell where one idea ends and the next begins.
isolation.instructions_ar: هذه هي السمة التي تجعل الجملة المشتقة مفهومة. أغلق الجملة المشتقة بوقفة صغيرة ثم ابدأ الجملة الرئيسية.
practice: Having finished the report | I went home
Seen from above | the city looks tiny

sentence_practice: Having finished the report, I went home early.
Arriving early, she waited in the lobby.
Having read the contract, he refused to sign.
daily_drills.record_this: Having finished the report well ahead of schedule, I went home early for once. Arriving nearly an hour early, she waited quietly in the lobby with her notes. Having read the contract properly, he refused to sign anything until the terms were changed.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'Having finished the report, I went home'. Is there a clear but short pause at the comma?

isolation.instructions: The negative goes first: 'NOT having received a reply…'. 'Not' takes the stress, then 'having' stays light. 'Being aware of the risk…' works the same way, with 'being' light and the following word stressed: /ˈbiːɪŋ/ aWARE.
isolation.instructions_ar: النفي يتقدّم: 'NOT having received a reply…'. 'Not' تأخذ النبر و'having' تبقى خفيفة، وكذلك 'Being aware…'.
practice: not is stressed, having stays light

pair: I did not know what to say, so…

sentence_practice: Not having received a reply, I called again.
Being aware of the risk, we proceeded carefully.
Not knowing what to say, he simply nodded.
daily_drills.record_this: Not having received a reply after four full days, I called the office again. Being fully aware of the risk involved, we proceeded very carefully with the trial. Not knowing quite what to say in the moment, he simply nodded and looked away.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'Not having received a reply'. Is 'not' first and stressed, with 'having' staying light?

mixed_pairs: When it is seen from above…
challenge_sentences: Having reviewed the file, I have some questions.
Given the circumstances, we acted correctly.
Having been informed late, they could do nothing.
Not knowing the answer, she asked for time.
daily_drills.record_this: Having reviewed the entire file this morning, I have a few questions for the team. Given the circumstances at the time, I still believe we acted correctly. Having been informed far too late, they could realistically do nothing about it. Not knowing the answer immediately, she sensibly asked for more time.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: light 'having', stress on the participle, and a clear short pause at the clause boundary.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself reading this account. Participle clauses make writing concise, so keep a steady pace and mark every boundary — then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تقرأ هذا النص. الجُمَل المشتقة تجعل الكتابة موجزة، فحافظ على إيقاع ثابت وحدّد كل وقفة، ثم اسمع وراجع.
test_yourself.passage: Having worked in this field for almost fifteen years, I have learnt to be cautious about early results. Seen from the outside, a promising first month can look like proof of everything. Given how much money often depends on that impression, the temptation to announce success early is enormous. Not having understood this myself at the start, I made exactly that mistake once, and having announced a result publicly, I then spent six months quietly correcting it. Being aware of the risk now, I hold announcements back until the data has settled. Faced with pressure from above, I explain the reasoning rather than simply refusing. Having been burned once, I would rather be slow than wrong. Written down like this, it sounds obvious. Learned the hard way, it took years.

sounds_to_check.light 'having' + stressed participle: Having WORKED…, having anNOUNCED…, Having BEEN burned
sounds_to_check.past-participle openers: SEEN from the outside, GIVEN how much money, FACED with pressure, WRITTEN down like this, LEARNED the hard way
sounds_to_check.boundary pause: Having worked in this field for almost fifteen years | I have learnt…
sounds_to_check.negative and 'being' openers: NOT having understood this myself…, /ˈbiːɪŋ/ aWARE of the risk now

scoring_guide.90_100: Light auxiliaries, stressed participles, every boundary clearly marked. Concise and highly readable. Ready for week 5.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasionally 'having' takes too much weight or a boundary is rushed.
scoring_guide.50_69: Boundaries missing, so clauses run together and meaning blurs. Repeat day 4, then days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5. Start with the boundary pause — it matters more than anything else here.

for_arabic_speakers: The boundary pause is not decoration. Without it, 'Having finished the report I went home' is genuinely hard to parse.
'Having' is light and quick /ˈhævɪŋ/. The stress belongs to the participle that follows it.
Always use the third form: 'having finished', never 'having finish'.
The negative comes first: 'Not having received…', not 'Having not received…'.
The subject of the participle clause must match the main clause. 'Having finished the report, the phone rang' wrongly says the phone finished the report.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; on day 7 listen specifically for the pause at each clause boundary.
